match.reason: The closest bank point, Scarcity, only lists the four factors of production as a supporting detail within a broader lesson on scarcity and opportunity cost, so no bank point teaches factors of production as its own idea.

draft.title: Factors of production
card: Factors of production are the resources used to make goods and services. There are four: natural resources, labour, capital and enterprise.
Natural resources
gifts of nature used in production, such as land, water, minerals and forests.
Labour
the physical and mental work people do. Capital means human-made goods used to make other goods, such as machines, tools and buildings. It is not money.
Enterprise

the skill of organising the other factors, taking risks and starting a business. The reward for each factor is income: wages for labour, rent for natural resources, interest for capital and profit for enterprise.
draft.remember: Natural resources, labour, capital and enterprise are the inputs. Capital is made goods, not money.

a.q: Mia buys an oven for her new bakery in Ballarat. Which factor of production is the oven?
a.why: An oven is a human-made good used to make other goods, so it is capital. It is not enterprise, which is the skill of organising and risk-taking, and it is not a natural resource because people made it.
a.clue: Was it made by people to help make other goods?

b.q: Tom borrows $50,000 and uses it to start a market garden near Shepparton. Which part of this case is enterprise?
opts: Tom organising the farm and taking the risk
The soil and water on the land
The tractor Tom buys for the farm
b.why: Enterprise is organising the other factors and taking the risk of starting a business, which is what Tom does. The loan is only money, which is not capital here. The soil is a natural resource and the tractor is capital.
b.clue: Which option is about a person's role in starting and running the business?

b.best: Tom organising the farm and taking the risk

problems.detail: Why (b) says the loan 'is not capital here'. The word 'here' suggests money can be capital in other cases, which contradicts the card's plain rule that capital 'is not money'.

The stem says Tom borrows $50,000 but never mentions a bank, yet the option calls it a 'loan from the bank'. A tractor also appears only in the options. This is minor, but the options add details the case does not give.
